note: Bundled fallback. The remote version is fetched every 12 hours and replaces this one if it has a higher version. Everything site-specific lives here — never in the code.

desktop.note:
Controls whether pairing with Vibly Desktop is offered in the interface, and whether the extension even tries to connect. False until the app can be downloaded from the product page — see architecture.md#distribution-lives-in-the-extension. It lives here rather than as a constant in the code precisely so it can be switched on without a new store submission: raise the version, push to vibly-registry, done within twelve hours.

Turning it off does not extinguish an existing pairing. The token and enabled stay in storage.local, so anyone already paired is connected again the moment the field becomes true — without running vibly-probe pair again.

The field must be a real boolean. The string "false" is truthy, and then a connection is offered to an app that does not exist; validate() in registry.js therefore rejects the remote file rather than guessing.

ai.label: Claude Code
ai.note: Placed BEFORE claude deliberately: providerForTabUrl takes the first hit, and claude's pattern matches /code/ too. The answer streams over WebSocket (wss://claude.ai/v1/sessions/ws/…/subscribe), which chrome.webRequest never sees — hence tier 2, the stop button, as the completion signal instead of the network. All three patterns are needed: `/code/*` does not match `/code`, and the entry point without a session is exactly where you land before choosing one.

verified.note:
ANSWER LENGTH, added 2026-08-28 after the working signal was still not enough. The requirement as stated: while the model works and narrates what it is doing, the volume stays up. It may only come down for the real answer. A signal that fires on the first character cannot do that, because narration and answer are the same markup — both are prose in .prose > .contents — and nothing structural separates them.

What separates them is length. The opening sentence in the reported turn ran to about 120 characters ("I will go deeper this time - reading the SQL functions and the game loop properly instead of just listing files"). The answer in the captured turn ran to 2760 characters across its containers, 1070 in the paragraph alone. A factor of 23 between them.

400 sits in that gap with 3.3x of headroom above the narration and 6.9x below the answer. It is a threshold and therefore a heuristic, which docs/architecture.md warns about — the warning is against thresholds that are guessed, and the two numbers behind this one are written above so the next person can judge them.

THE COST is that the duck arrives about 3.5 seconds into the answer rather than at its first character: the paragraph reached 482 characters at 26676 ms having started at 22543 ms. That is the price of never dipping during narration, and it was the stated preference.

THE FAILURE MODE is a real answer shorter than 400 characters, which never ducks at all. A one-line answer is also one nobody needs quiet to read, so this is deliberate rather than overlooked.

The counter resets whenever the tools speak, so a sentence before the commands never adds up with the answer after them.

cowork had no answerMinChars, on the reasoning that the answer is the only prose in its turns. That was wrong and is corrected 2026-08-29 — see its own entry: 149 characters of narration, tool work, then the answer. The premise held for the turns that had been measured, which is a different thing from holding.

WORKING CONTAINER, added 2026-08-28 after the first field turned out to rest on a false premise. Code does not write one answer: it writes a sentence, runs commands, then writes the real answer. The turn captured for answerText happened to put all its prose in one block at 22543 ms, so the interleaving was invisible in it — n=1 doing exactly what n=1 does.

What is observable is that the tools start again between the two stretches of prose. In the same capture button.group/tool grew from 7551 ms to 21396 ms and stopped before the answer began, with nothing after it. So workingText is the signal to bring the music back, and answerText is the signal to take it down; the turn can alternate between them as often as it likes.

The restore is the existing cancellable one, so a tool block that flickers inside a stretch of prose does not raise the volume — the next prose cancels it first.

group/tool is a Tailwind group name, not a hash. It survives a rebuild in a way _wordAnimating_fp3b6_12 does not.

NOT MEASURED: the interleaved turn itself. The handle comes from a turn that did not interleave, and the claim that these are the same tool rows is a reading of the screen rather than of a capture.

cowork deliberately has NO workingText — still true 2026-08-29, but no longer because it behaves correctly: it interleaves as much as Code does, and the reset is what would let its threshold rest on the narration alone. What stops the field being set is that the candidate is unmeasured on an interleaved turn, not that the need is absent. The obvious candidate is worse than nothing: [data-testid="session-status-line"] also grows at 64642 ms, after the answer is finished, which would raise the music exactly while it is being read.

ANSWER CONTAINER, measured 2026-08-28 over one agentic turn with tools/inspect-ai-provider.js. The stop button appeared 271 ms after the send and the first character of the answer arrived at 22543 ms — 22 seconds of tool work in between, the same shape as cowork and a different handle entirely.

CODE SHARES NO MARKUP WITH COWORK HERE. There is no .standard-markdown anywhere in the capture. The answer grows under div.prose > div.contents (p, h3, ul, ol, li, code, strong, a.prose-link all sit below it). The stop button and composer already differed — aria-label "Stop" against "Stop response", data-testid code-prompt-input against chat-input — so assuming one surface from the other would have failed here.

NOT .contents ALONE, and this is the trap in the data. Two elements carry that class. The working phase grows in div.flex.flex-col > div.contents > div.flex.flex-col at 7544 ms, fifteen seconds before the answer. They are told apart by their parent: only the answer's .contents sits directly under .prose. A selector of .contents would duck while the tools were still running, which is the fault this field exists to fix.

NOT _wordAnimating_fp3b6_12 either. CSS module hash, changes on any rebuild.

n=1, and one limitation worth naming: the instrument records three levels of ancestry, so it can say that .prose does not appear within three levels of any working-phase growth — it cannot prove no working-phase element sits under a .prose further up. If this ducks at around seven seconds rather than twenty-two, that is what happened.

The first value was measured while the environment was starting (provision, clone) — not representative. The button stayed up through the whole turn including tool calls, so there is no flicker risk between tools. Abort: the button was gone 208 ms after the click.

ai.label: Cowork
ai.note: Placed BEFORE claude deliberately, for the same reason as claude-code: providerForTabUrl takes the first hit, and claude's `*://claude.ai/*` matches /cowork/ too. Without its own entry Cowork inherits claude's network pattern, and that never fires — Cowork does not go through chat_conversations/*/completion. The consequence was not silence but something worse: the DOM send started the music, and ten seconds later the undo in noteUserSent fired and ducked in the middle of an answer still being written. Hence completion "dom" and confirmWithinMs 0, exactly like Claude Code. All three patterns are needed: `/cowork/*` does not match `/cowork`.

verified.streamTransport: not identified — but NOT WebSocket, and not a streamed fetch or XHR
verified.note:
ANSWER LENGTH, added 2026-08-29, and it reverses the paragraph that used to stand here. That paragraph said cowork needs no answerMinChars because the answer is the only prose in the turn. It is not. Measured 2026-08-28 over one agentic turn: 149 characters of narration written from 20603 ms, 9.75 seconds of tool work, then the answer from 30951 ms running to 462 characters. Ten seconds of music down for a sentence.

The narration also re-mounts its own paragraph 138 ms after writing it — 76 characters counted a second time — so what the counter actually sees before the answer is 225, not 149. 320 is the geometric mean of 225 and 462: equal relative headroom either way, 1.42x. It is the honest centre of two measurements rather than a round number, and the two numbers are written above so the next person can judge it.

THE HEADROOM IS THIN, and much thinner than claude-code's, where 120 against 2760 leaves a factor of 23. Here it is a factor of two. A turn that narrates twice as much as this one ducks early; an answer shorter than 320 characters never ducks at all. The second is deliberate on the same grounds as Code — a one-line answer is one nobody needs quiet to read — and the first is the reason workingText is worth measuring here. The counter resets whenever the tools speak, which would leave the narration as the only floor. [data-testid="tool-row-caret"] and p.pl-1.text-muted are the candidates: measured 2026-08-28 growing only in the working phase and stopping 10.7 s before the answer. NOT measured on the interleaved turn itself, so the field is not set.

NOT [data-testid="session-status-line"] as the working handle, for the second time with numbers: it grew at 36315 ms after the send in one capture, 7.7 seconds AFTER the answer had begun. As a working signal it would raise the music exactly while it is being read.

RE-MOUNTING, measured 2026-08-28 with a probe mirroring grewInside branch for branch. The transcript is virtualised, and an older turn's .standard-markdown arrives in the DOM again, whole. 1043 and 44 characters, four times each inside one turn, byte-identical every time — text being written never grows by the same amount twice. The first arrival came seconds after the send and 27 seconds before the answer, and under the registry of the day Vibly ducked on it.

Every re-mount was NOT the last container in document order, and every real one was. That is the fix, and it is in the code rather than here because it is a fact about virtualised feeds and not about Cowork: ai-sensor.js counts an arriving container only when it is the newest on the page. tools/verify-answer-mount.mjs holds the measured sequence and fails against the old branch.

Two turns captured with tools/inspect-ai-provider.js, Chrome 151, English interface.

THE STOP BUTTON CARRIES NO data-testid, and the claim that it did was wrong. Measured 2026-08-27 by reading the live element off a turn in progress: <button type="button" data-cds="Button" data-cds-icon-only data-cds-ghost class="cds-reset …" aria-label="Stop response" id="_r_p2_" data-trigger-disabled>. No data-testid on it at all, the id is generated per render, and the seven ancestors up to the composer are anonymous divs without one either. aria-label is the only handle the element offers.

The move to button[data-testid="chat-input-stop"] on 2026-08-26 therefore removed the only working selector and Cowork stopped ducking entirely. The shape to recognise: under tier 2 there is no network signal to fall back on, and confirmWithinMs 0 means no undo either. The send is still detected and the music still comes up, the console goes on printing sent: enter, and nothing ever brings it down again for the life of the tab.

The superseded paragraph is not kept, because its reasoning does not survive. It argued that the testid and the label were two handles on the same element and that the testid was the better one. Only the second half was ever a judgement; the first was a reading, and the reading was wrong. What the capture of 2026-08-26 actually matched was never established.

So cowork is back on an English aria-label, alongside claude-code, and that is a cost rather than a preference: if this interface is localised, detection here does not lose precision, it stops. Copilot stays the one tier 2 provider with a language-independent handle. No structural alternative exists on Cowork today — it was looked for.

tools/verify-stop-selectors.mjs holds the measured markup as a fixture and asserts this field against it. verify-stop-settle.mjs cannot: it stubs querySelector by comparing the selector to itself, so a selector that matches nothing on the real page passes it every time. That is how this got through.

THE TRANSPORT IS NOT WEBSOCKET. The previous entry left that open and it can now be closed one notch further: the capture hooked fetch, XHR and WebSocket and caught zero sockets and zero streamed responses across 115 s covering two whole answers. The only session request at the send is POST /v1/code/sessions/<id>/events, 221 bytes, not streamed. What carries the answer is something none of those three hooks see — EventSource is the obvious candidate and is NOT tested. The conclusion for the entry is unchanged but now rests on a reading instead of an inference: there is no network signal to be had, so completion is dom and confirmWithinMs is 0.

THE STOP BUTTON IS NOT THE ANSWER HERE, and that is the whole reason answerText exists. Measured 2026-08-28 over one agentic turn with tools/inspect-ai-provider.js: the button appeared 273 ms after the send, and the first character of the actual answer arrived at 50820 ms. Fifty and a half seconds of tool work in between, during which duckAt on-response-start had the music down for nothing.

The handle is the container the answer is written into. All six growing elements belonging to the answer sat under .standard-markdown (p.font-claude-response-body, ul, li, strong, a). Not one working-phase element did: those are [data-testid="session-status-line"], [data-testid="tool-row-caret"], .timeline-status-layer and p.pl-1.text-muted.

NOT the hashed siblings. _blocks_fp3b6_47 and _animating_fp3b6_10 are CSS module hashes and change on any rebuild — the same class of mistake that removed the only working stop button selector on 2026-08-26. .standard-markdown and .font-claude-response-body are the two unhashed names on offer; the outer one is used because it covers the list and inline elements too.

n=1, and one surface. Whether tool output that renders as markdown also lands in .standard-markdown was NOT observed, and that is how this would go wrong — ducking early, though by seconds rather than by fifty. claude-code is unmeasured and deliberately carries no answerText.

The button appeared 380 ms and 268 ms after the send and stood for 4.6 s and 56.1 s, with no flicker in either turn — unlike copilot.

Superseded 2026-08-26 (kept because the reasoning still holds): Measured by the user in a real session (claude.ai/cowork/cse_…) while an answer was streaming: claude's selector button[aria-label="Stop response"] hits, and the button stayed up while the answer was written. The composer field was not read separately, but the DOM send already worked while Cowork inherited claude — so div[data-testid="chat-input"] carries here too. That the transport is invisible is the conclusion from the undo firing: no request confirmed the send within 10 s. Whether it is WebSocket as in Claude Code is NOT settled. Timing values are absent on purpose — they are not measured, and a guessed figure would have looked like a measurement.

THE INTERLEAVED TURN, measured 2026-09-01, and it closes the hole the paragraph at the end of this note left open. Two turns captured with tools/inspect-ai-provider.js, Chrome 151, English interface.

The second one is the measurement. Response headers at 863 ms; the tools then wrote for half a minute across four separate stretches; the first character of the answer at 37712 ms. THIRTY-SEVEN SECONDS, which is six times the previous worst reading in answerLagsNetworkMs and the clearest case yet for why the headers are not the answer signal. The first turn of the same capture lagged 6575 ms.

THE ENTRY BEHAVED, and that is the point of recording a turn nobody had to fix. workingText (button[class~="group/row"], p.pl-1.text-muted) grew at 7002, 9892, 17021 and 20026 ms after the send and NEVER AFTER THE ANSWER BEGAN — the last of them 17.7 seconds ahead of it. Nothing grew inside .standard-markdown during the whole working phase, so the counter met the answer at zero and 160 was reached 632 ms after the first character.

THE TAG IN button[class~="group/row"] IS LOAD-BEARING, and this capture is the first evidence of it. a.group/row.flex grew 65 characters at 13583 ms — a chat-history link in the sidebar, carrying the same Tailwind group name as the tool row. The selector names `button`, so it does not match. Written down because a later tidy-up to a bare .group/row would look harmless and would not be: sidebar links grow when the conversation list updates, which is NOT bound to the working phase, and workingText raises the music. Whether such a link ever grows mid-answer is not measured; the tag makes it moot.

MID-STREAM SILENCE IS WORSE THAN RECORDED. maxMidStreamGapMs was 3864 from 2026-07-31 and is now 6690, measured on the agentic turn; the quieter turn of the same capture reached 5774. The field is the argument for the heuristic tier being off here, so it stands corrected upward rather than left as the friendlier number.

Extended thinking gives several seconds of network silence mid-answer — hence heuristics off. Re-measured 2026-07-31 over three turns, one of them aborted: nine pauses over 500 ms in a single answer, the longest 3864 ms.

THE ANSWER CONTAINER, added 2026-08-29, and claude is the FIRST provider to carry one alongside a network pattern. Reported from a real session: under duckAt on-response-start the music went down as soon as Claude started a web search, and stayed down through the whole search. Measured with tools/inspect-ai-provider.js over three turns, then a second time with a probe mirroring grewInside branch for branch.

The numbers on the search turn, from Enter: request out at 25 ms, stop button at 329 ms, RESPONSE HEADERS AT 1293 ms — which is where Vibly ducked — the tool row growing at 2844 ms, and the first character of the actual answer at 7297 ms. Six seconds of quiet for a search nobody was reading. The other two turns in the same capture lagged by 1939 ms and 228 ms, so the fault scales with how much work the turn does and disappears on a turn that does none.

WHY THE FIELD ALONE WOULD NOT HAVE HELPED: onResponseBegan fired regardless, twenty seconds before the text. The rule that a measured answerText outranks the network response signal is in ai-detector.js, and tools/verify-answer-outranks-network.mjs holds it.

NOT THE HASHED SIBLINGS. The answer streams into span._animating_fp3b6_10 inside p.font-claude-response-body inside div._blocks_fp3b6_47.standard-markdown. _animating_fp3b6_10 and _blocks_fp3b6_47 are CSS module hashes and change on any rebuild — the same class of mistake that removed cowork's only working stop button selector on 2026-08-26. .standard-markdown is the unhashed name, and it is the same handle cowork uses: claude.ai and Cowork share a design system, which claude-code does not.

ANSWER LENGTH 160, the geometric mean of two figures rather than a round number. THE FLOOR has two parts and the higher one wins. The measured part is 82 characters of warmup: on the first turn after a page load div[class] render-path-warmup renders markup inside .standard-markdown, and the probe counted 14 chars at 220 ms and 68 more at 350 ms before anything had been answered. The larger part is NOT measured on this surface and is carried over from Code as a prior — an opening narration sentence there ran to about 120 characters, and the same model writing the same kind of sentence here is a reasonable expectation but not a reading. THE CEILING is measured: the short answer on the search turn of the first capture, about 215 characters. sqrt(120 x 215) = 160, which leaves 1.33x of headroom either way.

THE HEADROOM IS THIN, thinner than claude-code's factor of 23 and about the same as cowork's 1.42x. A no-tools turn that renders more warmup than this one ducks early; a real answer shorter than 130 characters never ducks at all. The second is deliberate on the same grounds as Code and Cowork — a one-line answer is one nobody needs quiet to read — and it is now caught by the end-of-turn fallback in index.js, which claude can afford because it has a completion signal and they do not.

WORKING CONTAINER, and it is what makes the thin headroom safe on the turn that matters: the tools speak at 1850 ms, AFTER all 82 characters of warmup and 4.4 seconds before the answer, so the counter is reset to zero and the answer is measured from nothing. Observed in the probe as `TOOLS (+34) raknaren 82 -> 0`, then two more resets at 2960 ms.

BOTH SELECTORS WERE MEASURED AS ONE, and neither was isolated. The probe ran them as a list and the log does not say which of the two matched. p.pl-1.text-muted sits inside button.group/row in the capture, so the button alone would probably cover it — probably is not measured, so the list stays as it was tested. group/row is a Tailwind group name, which survives a rebuild in a way a hash does not; pl-1 and text-muted are utility classes and are the weaker half.

NOT span.timeline-status-layer, which grew at 6573 ms on the search turn — 700 ms BEFORE the answer began, and it would have raised the music just as it needed to come down. It is the same trap [data-testid="session-status-line"] was on cowork, twice.

n=2 captures, one surface, English interface, Chrome 151. What is NOT measured: a turn that interleaves prose, tools and more prose the way Claude Code does. Both captured search turns put the tools before the answer and nothing after.

ai.label: ChatGPT
ai.note: The exclusion takes everything with one further slash. The completion stream sits directly on /f/conversation with no following path, while /f/conversation/prepare is an ordinary POST that fires within a second of the stream closing — without the exclusion it reads as a new generation and the music comes back at the very moment it should be ducked. The shape is deliberately broad: it also covers future sub-paths. Unlike claude, the abort sits on its own path and therefore needs no exclusion.

verified.note:
THE ANSWER CONTAINER, added 2026-09-01, and it closes a gap this entry carried from the start. Under `duckAt: on-response-start` chatgpt ducked on the response headers, which say the turn began and not that the answer did — the same fault claude had until 2026-08-29.

Measured with tools/inspect-ai-provider.js over three turns, Chrome 151, Swedish interface. From the response headers to the first character inside the container: 632 ms on a one-line turn, 277 ms on a 3243-character turn, and 2460 ms on a turn that searched the web and drew a chart. The fault scales with how much work the turn does, exactly as on claude — but an order of magnitude smaller, because this search took two seconds where claude's took six.

.streaming-animation AND NOT .markdown. The answer streams into div.streaming-animation.markdown and is swapped for div.markdown.prose when the turn ends — measured at 9483 ms on turn 2 and 5547 ms on turn 3, both after the last streamed character. Only the in-flight answer carries streaming-animation, so an older turn re-mounting as .markdown.prose cannot reach this selector at all. That matters here for the reason it mattered on cowork: .markdown.prose holds every previous answer in the transcript, and .markdown alone would match them all. Neither name is hashed — wcDTda_prosemirror-parent and YlkxtG_TransitionItem in the same capture are, and are avoided as everywhere else.

NO answerMinChars, and that is a reading rather than an omission. On cowork and claude the field exists because narration and answer share the markup. Here they do not. Across three turns, including the one that searched, NOTHING was written inside the answer container before the answer itself: the working narration is a 33-character span.loading-shimmer-tertiary in a sibling subtree at 1383 ms, and the search result is a recharts widget under div.puik-root.not-prose, which the class name says outright. The measured floor is zero, so the threshold falls to 1 in ai-sensor.js — announce the first character. The shortest real answer in the capture ran to about 17 characters, which a threshold carried over from claude would have silenced entirely.

THE REASONING TURN IS NOW MEASURED, and it is what the field rested on. Two further turns the same day, on a second capture: the chain-of-thought UI rendered — data-testid="cot-v5-tool-icon-pile" and cot-v5-favicon, alongside button[aria-label="Söker på 2 webbplatser"] — and the reasoning quota fell from 2 to 1 across the first of them. The headers landed at 794 ms and the first character of the answer at 11117 ms: 10.3 seconds of thinking and searching, and NOT ONE CHARACTER of it inside .streaming-animation. The turn without tools was 1448 ms early on the same measure.

WHERE THE THINKING GOES INSTEAD, and every one of these is a sibling subtree: div.fKQ0lq_Layout > div.fKQ0lq_TransitionItem at 2086 ms carrying 107 characters, the cot-v5 icon pile at 2903 ms, span.loading-shimmer-tertiary at 2989 ms with 61 characters, and the search button at 3275 ms. The reading that the container is clean therefore holds for narration, tools AND thinking, which is the strongest case any provider here has for shipping without a threshold. It also settles the earlier note in this entry, which read the quota line but not what it implied.

THE COT CONTAINERS ARE HASHED — fKQ0lq_Layout, fKQ0lq_TransitionItem, YlkxtG_TransitionItem, WlXitW_TransitionGroupChild — so none of them is a handle. The unhashed names in that subtree are the cot-v5 testids, and they are noted for whoever measures workingText properly.

MATH AND TABLES ARE ANSWER CONTENT and land inside the container as they should: span[role="math"] at 3045 ms with its span.katex-display, and div.group.TyagGW_tableContainer at 14886 ms. The hashed table class is inside the answer rather than a handle for it, so it costs nothing.

THE WORKING CONTAINER IS STILL NOT SET, now on n=2. span.loading-shimmer-tertiary.text-token-text-tertiary grew once per tool turn and never after the answer: 33 characters at 1383 ms in the first capture, 61 at 2989 ms in the second, 1844 ms and 8128 ms ahead of the answer respectively. That is a good candidate and not yet a measurement of the case that matters — neither turn interleaved prose, tools and more prose, so nothing here shows what it does AFTER an answer has begun. That is the direction the field fails in, and it is how session-status-line broke cowork twice. With the threshold at 1 there is no counter for it to reset either, so setting it would buy only the music coming back up mid-turn. Not worth it yet.

THE COMPOSER WAS NOT RE-READ. The capture's only composer candidate was div[aria-label="Chatta med ChatGPT"] — Swedish, and therefore useless as a selector. #prompt-textarea stands as it did on 2026-08-03; the report neither confirms nor refutes it, and the send worked throughout. THE STOP BUTTON is re-confirmed: button[data-testid="stop-button"], appearing 507, 313 and 316 ms after the send, with aria-label "Sluta svara" on this machine — which is the reason the testid is the handle.

No abort turn in this capture, so the abort pattern rests on the measurement that follows.

Three turns: short, long and one aborted. The selectors are language-independent — data-testid and id respectively — which is better than claude's English aria-label. The signal order is the reverse of claude's: here the DOM is consistently faster, by 1000 ms on the short answer and 312 ms on the long one, so the lead shrinks with length instead of growing. The network is still the primary signal, because it is the truth about when the stream closed, and the half second disappears into the 1200 ms grace period. The abort: stop_conversation fired 31 ms after the click and the completion stream died early after 18 chunks instead of ending with [DONE].

ai.label: Gemini
ai.note:
THE ANSWER CONTAINER, added 2026-09-01, and gemini is the last provider here to get one. It also has the longest silent stretch of any surface that is not agentic: a thinking phase runs before every answer, and the first character arrived 7996, 13360 and 14607 ms after the send across three turns. A fourth was stopped during thinking and never answered at all.

THE THINKING TEXT IS OUTSIDE THE PANEL, which is what makes this cheap. It grows in div.thinking-container > div[data-testid="thinking-overlay-content"] > span, and thinking-overlay is a SIBLING of structured-content-container rather than an ancestor of the markdown panel. Measured at 7369 ms on the first turn and three times each on the next two. So the container is clean and there is NO answerMinChars, the same reading as chatgpt and perplexity.

NOT `.markdown-main-panel` ON ITS OWN, and this is the fourth surface to need that care. When a new turn starts, the previous answer is re-rendered into the persistent conversation container: div.markdown.markdown-main-panel > p gained 6368 characters 64 ms after the third send and 2230 characters 121 ms after the fourth. A bare panel selector ducks there, before the turn it belongs to has thought a single thought.

THE STREAMING MARKER IS THE HANDLE. Gemini tags text as it arrives — p.pending, span.pending, b.pending, ul.pending, li.pending, p.animating, p.first-token.animating — and DROPS those classes when the turn finishes. Every re-mount above landed in a plain p with no marker at all. `.markdown-main-panel .pending` therefore reaches the answer being written and cannot reach one that is already written, which is the same shape as chatgpt's .streaming-animation. Neither class is hashed.

THE COMPOSER AND THE MISSING STOP BUTTON ARE BOTH RECONFIRMED, and the entry was right about the reason. The button is button[aria-label="Stoppa svar"] — Swedish — with no data-testid, and its class string is byte-identical to the send button's for the whole 160 characters the instrument records: both are mdc-icon-button mat-mdc-icon-button mat-mdc-button-base mat-badge mat-unthemed mat-badge-overlap mat-badge-above mat-badge-after mat-badge-small mat-badge-hidde[n]. There is still no language-independent selector to write. The composer offered div[aria-label="Ange en prompt för Gemini"] as its first candidate, which is localised; .ql-editor stands, and ql-clipboard was again a sibling without it.

THE ABORT IS RECONFIRMED AND THE NUMBERS MOVED. The stop click at 3671 ms was followed by rpcids=NkpXw 18 ms later, against 3 ms on 2026-08-04, and the StreamGenerate XHR closed 522 ms after the click rather than 1740. The signal is still worth its own pattern; the margin it buys is smaller than it was.

THE SEND FIRES TWICE in this instrument on gemini and only here: Enter is seen, and the send button click that Angular raises from it is seen 4 to 6 ms later. That is the tool, not the provider — Vibly debounces the send — but it is worth writing down before someone reads two SENDs as two turns.

No networkExclude is needed. The noise sits on /_/BardChatUi/data/batchexecute (rpcids ESY5D, VxUbXb, aPya6c, PCck7e) which fires both during and after the stream, but only shares the prefix /_/BardChatUi/data/ — the full RPC path to StreamGenerate tells them apart without an exclusion. PCck7e was added 2026-08-27 on a single sighting, about three seconds before StreamGenerate opened. The list is observed noise, not a closed set, and that is exactly why the pattern names StreamGenerate instead of excluding what happens to be known. The pattern must not pin hl=: that parameter carries the interface language and was hl=sv in the measurement.

No stopButton, deliberately. Gemini labels the button only with a localised aria-label ("Stoppa svar"), has no data-testid, and shares every single class with the send button — mdc-icon-button mat-mdc-icon-button mat-mdc-button-base ... are identical strings for both. There is simply no language-independent selector to write. The field is only read when completion is "dom" (ai-sensor.js), and Gemini has a network signal, so it would be dead weight and a trap: the day someone switches completion here, detection would silently stop working for everyone except Swedish users.

input is Quill's own class rather than the localised aria-label ("Ange en prompt för Gemini") for the same reason. ql-clipboard is a sibling node without ql-editor, so .ql-editor hits only the real field.

The abort was measured 2026-08-04 and sits on batchexecute with rpcids=NkpXw — an RPC that occurred exactly once in the whole capture, 3 ms after the stop click. It is worth its own signal: the stream lived another 1740 ms after the click, so without abort the duck would only release 2940 ms after the user pressed, grace period included.

The pattern does not pin the parameter order (batchexecute*rpcids=NkpXw*) and therefore holds even if rpcids moves within the query string or is batched with other calls. The RPC id is Google's and can change with a server rollout; if it stops matching the consequence is merely the old 1200 ms grace period, not broken detection. An overlap with network is impossible — StreamGenerate and batchexecute are separate RPC paths.

verified.note:
Four turns on a Swedish interface. The network is consistently ahead of the DOM by 231–797 ms, i.e. the same order as claude and the opposite of chatgpt. Enter to request is 15–30 ms, considerably steadier than claude's span of up to 4081 ms.

The stop button appeared after 2500 ms in the first turn and 290–299 ms in the three that followed — the same pattern as claude-code, where the first measurement was taken before the page was warm. It is unused here regardless.

The stream goes over XHR, not fetch. The inspection tool does no gap analysis on XHR, so pauses mid-answer are unmeasured even though a reasoning prompt was run. That is immaterial to the entry since the heuristic is off and the network signal is the stream's actual close — but it means we do not know whether Gemini goes silent for several seconds mid-answer, and that is needed before the heuristic is ever switched on here.

The abort measurement of 2026-08-04 gave ONLY ONE valid point, not two. After the first stop, Gemini's interface stopped sending StreamGenerate: two subsequent sends were registered as SEND but produced zero requests over 20 seconds, and the stop button never disappeared from the DOM during the whole capture. The second stop click therefore hit a button with no stream behind it and only fired ESY5D. Vibly takes no harm from that — noteAborted returns without action when no requests are in flight — but abortRpcId rests on n=1 and deserves confirming the next time anyone measures Gemini.

ai.label: Perplexity
ai.note:
The pattern MUST name perplexity_ask explicitly. The prefix /rest/sse/ is not the answer's alone: under the same prefix sits recent_thread_updates, a long-lived SSE stream that in the measurement stayed open for 47 seconds, spanned three turns and kept itself alive with a ping every fifteen seconds. A pattern on /rest/sse/* would have read it as a running generation and held the music ducked continuously — a failure that looks like the duck never releasing. Where chatgpt needed networkExclude to tell sibling paths apart, the full path suffices here.

The abort also sits under /rest/sse/, on perplexity_terminate, and fired 18 ms after the stop click. Its own path, so no exclusion — but it is the second reason never to broaden network to the prefix.

One turn is ONE stream. Perplexity's multi-step search happens inside the same SSE stream (search_implementation_mode: multi_step), not as separate requests, so there is no risk of the music bouncing between search and answer steps.

input is #ask-input — an id, so language-independent. A better handle than either claude or gemini has.

No stopButton, for the same reason as gemini: aria-label is the only workable selector ("Stop response (Esc)") and the classes are Tailwind utility classes shared with other buttons. The label was English despite a Swedish machine, which suggests Perplexity does not localise — but that is not verified, and the field is only read when completion is "dom" anyway.

verified.note:
THE ANSWER CONTAINER, added 2026-09-01, and perplexity had the widest gap of any surface here. Every turn searches before it answers, so there is no turn without a working phase and the fault never hides. Measured over three turns with tools/inspect-ai-provider.js, Chrome 151, Swedish interface: SSE response headers at 2366 ms and the first character of the answer at 6148 ms on a plain question, and headers at 2131 ms against an answer at 30366 ms on a multi-step one. TWENTY-EIGHT SECONDS on the second, where the search was 93 percent of the turn.

NOT `.prose`, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE CARE HERE. The obvious container is div.prose.dark:prose-invert, and it would be a REGRESSION rather than a fix. KaTeX hydrates lazily and long after its own turn closed: span.katex-display inside an EARLIER turn's .prose gained 96 characters at a time on seventeen occasions spread over 39 seconds, and one of them landed 101 ms after the NEXT send. Under `.prose` that is a duck 101 ms into a turn whose answer was half a minute away — earlier than the 2131 ms headers it was meant to replace.

The re-mount guard in ai-sensor.js does NOT catch it. That rule covers a container arriving whole and asks whether it is the newest on the page; this is growth INSIDE a container that was already there, which is a different branch, and the older turn is the newest .prose on the page anyway while the new turn has written nothing yet.

`.prose p` is the selector because the maths is not in a paragraph. It sits in .prose > div.overflow-x-auto > div > span.katex-display, so a paragraph-scoped selector cannot reach it, and every character of both measured answers arrived in p — directly, or inside strong, span.citation.inline and the p within li. THE COST is a turn answered entirely in a table or a formula: it would never announce and would fall back to the end of the turn. perplexity can afford that because it has a network completion signal, unlike the tier 2 surfaces. NOT MEASURED, because no captured turn was shaped that way. tools/verify-stop-selectors.mjs holds the katex path as `lateGrowth` and fails against `.prose`.

NO answerMinChars. Nothing grew inside .prose p before the answer on any of the three turns — the search steps write to span.min-w-0.truncate inside a hashed _sharedDuration_orhia_1 wrapper, well outside the prose. Measured floor zero, the same reading as chatgpt, so the threshold falls to 1.

PERPLEXITY DOES LOCALISE, and the paragraph below saying it does not is WRONG. That paragraph read an English "Stop response (Esc)" on a Swedish machine and inferred no localisation. Measured 2026-09-01 on the same kind of machine, the button is button[aria-label="Stoppa svar (Esc)"]. The inference was drawn from a single reading and it did not hold. stopButton therefore stays unset, but for a better reason than before: the only handle the element offers is a localised label, and the classes around it are shared Tailwind utilities. It costs nothing — the field is read only when completion is "dom", and perplexity is tier 1.

THE ABORT IS RECONFIRMED: the stop click at 14936 ms, perplexity_terminate out 15 ms later, the stream closing 390 ms after that. #ask-input is reconfirmed as the composer and is still an id.

Three turns: short, long and one aborted. Pro was unavailable, so reasoning mode is unmeasured.

Unlike gemini the stream goes over fetch, so the gap analysis works and the pauses mid-answer are ACTUALLY MEASURED: longest gap 2405 ms in the long turn. That is below claude's 3864 ms but well over a second, and confirms the heuristic should be off here — now on measurement rather than on caution.

The network leads the DOM by 109–298 ms, measured as stream:end to stopbutton:disappear. The same order as claude and gemini, the opposite of chatgpt.

Enter to request is 6–10 ms, the steadiest of all providers so far. The stop button appeared after 2059 ms in the first turn and 1105–1161 ms in the following ones — the same warm-up pattern as claude-code and gemini.

The abort closes the stream 688 ms after terminate fired. The tail of an ABORTED stream is indistinguishable from a finished one: both end with status COMPLETED, final_sse_message and event: end_of_stream. A sentinel-based tap could therefore not have told an abort from a finished answer — immaterial today since the tap is off for every AI provider, but it is the reason abort sits on the network and not on the tail.

ai.label: Copilot
ai.note:
THE ANSWER CONTAINER, added 2026-09-01, and copilot is the only tier 2 surface to get one. With no network to fall back on, buttonIsTheAnswer in ai-detector.js made the stop button the response signal — and the button says the turn began. Measured over four turns with tools/inspect-ai-provider.js, Chrome 151, Swedish interface: the button appeared 330, 688, 672 and 867 ms after the send, and the first character of the answer at 1567, 944, 3640 and 3880 ms. The two web-search turns were about three seconds early.

COPILOT NEEDS A THRESHOLD, and it is the first surface since cowork to. chatgpt and perplexity ship without one because nothing writes into their answer container before the answer; here the tool status row does. It lives at div.relative.isolate > div.overflow-hidden.pb-1 INSIDE the message body, and it wrote 26, 5, 54 and 45 characters before the answer on the four turns. With the threshold at 1 the duck would fire at 1611 ms on the search turn — two seconds before the answer, which is the fault in miniature.

answerMinChars 168 = sqrt(54 x 522), the geometric mean of the measured floor and the shortest complete answer in the capture. That leaves 3.1x either way, the widest headroom of any threshold in this registry (cowork has 1.4, claude 1.3). Checked against all four turns: the duck lands 96, 621, 771 and 515 ms after the first character.

SCOPED TO highlighted-chats, AND THAT IS THE RE-MOUNT GUARD. Copilot moves a finished turn from [data-testid="highlighted-chats"] into [data-testid="backstage-chats"] when the next one starts: a whole ai-message arrived there carrying 3436 characters 85 ms after the third send, and 3779 more 163 ms after the fourth. An unscoped [data-testid="ai-message-body"] would find that container inside the arriving node.

The newest-container rule in ai-sensor.js would PROBABLY catch it, and probably is the reason not to lean on it. The rule compares the arriving container to the last match in document order, so it holds only if backstage precedes highlighted in the DOM. That is what the names suggest and it is NOT read anywhere in the capture. Scoping the selector makes the question moot, which is the same choice perplexity made against its lazily-hydrating maths on the same day.

THE FLICKER IS RECONFIRMED, and this capture holds the whole mechanism rather than just the symptom. The first send of the conversation was met by a hashcash challenge over the socket: challenge at 489 ms, challengeResponse at 593 ms, the same send frame repeated at 594 ms, THE BUTTON GONE AT 620 ms AND BACK AT 903 ms. 283 ms, against 357 ms on 2026-08-09. STOP_SETTLE_MS is 800 and absorbs both, the tighter one with 443 ms to spare and this one with 517.

Turns 2, 3 and 4 of the same conversation got no challenge and no flicker, which sharpens the old note: it is not sessions that flicker, it is A CONVERSATION'S FIRST SEND. Two of three first sends across two captures. Still not every one, so it stays a thing that strikes intermittently.

THE SOCKET IS MEASURED FOR THE FIRST TIME, and every claim made about it from inference now has a reading. One socket, opened 263 ms after the first send and living through all four turns: 502 inbound frames, 15 outbound. The sentinel "event":"done" appears exactly where the entry said, after partCompleted, and titleUpdate follows it on the first turn — the trap the entry warned about, now seen. Keepalive is ping/pong and the longest idle gap was 5227 ms.

THE STOP GOES OVER THE SOCKET as {"event":"stop"}, sent 2 ms after the click, and no request accompanies it. That is why there is no abort field, now read rather than inferred. The button disappeared 164 ms after the click.

THE ARIA-LABEL IS "Avbrottsmeddelande" on this machine, which is Swedish and a poor description of the button besides. data-testid remains the only sane handle, and the same goes for the composer.

There is NO network signal to be had. The answer streams over wss://copilot.microsoft.com/c/api/chat, which chrome.webRequest never sees — the same situation as claude-code, i.e. tier 2 with the stop button as the completion signal. Hence also confirmWithinMs: 0: there is no completion request that can confirm the send, and the undo in noteUserSent would have waited for something that never comes.

NEVER try to add a network pattern here. The same origin carries two things that fire in quick succession during and after the stream: /cl/eus-b/collect (telemetry, eleven times over three turns) and /c/api/conversations/<id>/autosuggest (fires while typing, before Enter). A pattern on *://copilot.microsoft.com/* or on /c/api/* catches both and reads them as generation. The trap is written up in verify-provider-patterns.mjs.

The selectors are data-testid in both cases, so language-independent. That is worth saying explicitly: the button's aria-label was "Avbrottsmeddelande" on a Swedish machine, so a label-based selector would have worked only in Swedish. The same testid chatgpt uses, which is coincidence and not kinship.

The stop button CAN FLICKER at the start of a turn, and does so unpredictably. The send is sometimes met by a hashcash challenge: the client answers with challengeResponse and resends the same message, and the interface resets the button in between — gone for 357 ms in the measurement of 2026-08-09. A second run the same day, also a new conversation, got no challenge at all and no flicker. That it strikes intermittently is the reason to take it seriously rather than dismiss it: a failure that happens sometimes is harder to understand than one that always does. STOP_SETTLE_MS in ai-sensor.js is 800 ms and absorbs those 357 with 443 ms to spare. Shrink it and Copilot breaks first, and only sometimes.

No abort field. The stop goes over the same WebSocket as {"event":"stop"}, not as a request, so there is no URL to match. The button disappears 66 ms after the click and carries the signal alone.

If anyone later builds a tier 1.5 tap: the socket is ONE and lives through the whole session, across every turn. It opens on the FIRST send, not at page load — measured twice, 278 and 347 ms after Enter. Opening and closing are therefore not turn boundaries.

The turn is startMessage → (toolExecuting/citation on web search) → appendText → partCompleted → done. The sentinel is done, measured 2026-08-09. Two traps around it. The first: the sentinel is NOT the same as the last frame before silence. On a conversation's first turn, titleUpdate follows AFTER done, and after that pong keeps the socket alive every thirty seconds. A tap looking for silence rather than for done finds the wrong boundary, or none. The second: the string done is short and occurs in ordinary text, so the sentinel is "event":"done" and nothing shorter.

A tap would lead the DOM by about 234 ms — done on the socket against the button disappearing. Real but modest; it is not that gain which would justify a tap here but not having to depend on a button that flickers.

verified.flickerInSessions: 2 of 3, both on a conversation's first send
verified.note:
Two sessions. The first: three turns — short, long and one aborted, with the stop last. The second: two long turns without an abort, run to answer what the first could not. Swedish interface, Chrome 151, signed-in Microsoft account.

THE SENTINEL IS done. {"event":"done","messageId":"…"} followed by 10901 ms of silence. It came 234 ms before the stop button disappeared, which is what a tap would gain.

PAUSES MID-STREAM ARE NOW MEASURED: longest 2423 ms, after partCompleted in the last turn. During the stream there was also a pause of 1521 ms while the web search ran. Both are well over a second and confirm the heuristic should be off here — now on measurement rather than on caution. Distinguish them from 27250 ms, which is silence BETWEEN turns and not within one.

One turn is ONE stream. The web search happens inside it — toolExecuting with tool.type webSearch, then a citation event — not as separate requests. The same answer Perplexity gave to the same question, so no risk of the music bouncing between search and answer steps.

The button appeared 466 ms after Enter in the first turn and 721–727 ms in the two that followed — the reverse of claude-code, gemini and perplexity, where the FIRST turn was the slow one. The reason shows in the timeline: the challenge in turn one made the button come early, disappear and come back, while the later turns had a single clean rise.

The flicker is the turn's most important measurement: gone at 743 ms after send, back at 1100 ms. Without the settle window it would have read as a finished answer and ducked the music a second into a turn that took fourteen.

The button appeared 466–982 ms after Enter across five turns. No warm-up effect as with the other providers; the spread does not follow the turn order.

The abort: the stop click gave {"event":"stop"} on the socket after 2 ms and the button was gone after 66 ms. Faster than every other provider, but that measures DOM against DOM and not against a stream closing, so the number is not comparable with perplexity's 688 ms.

music.label: Spotify
music.note: The audio element is a detached <video> (Widevine/EME). Requires media-tap in MAIN world. Does not restore the volume itself — no adapter needed.

music.label: YouTube Music
music.note: The same player family as youtube — `#movie_player` exists here too — and the same signature: writes back its own saved value in a single jump. Differs in doing it intermittently rather than on an even cycle.

verified.note: Eight attempts, measured in isolation with Vibly out of the picture: the volume was set to 0.15 directly on the element and then we observed who touched it. Three wrote back, always to 1.0 which is the player's saved value and never to the value before the change. Three took no action at all within 35-40 s. Two were discarded because the track changed during the measurement — YouTube Music swaps media element on track change and the volume then restarts at 1.0, which is a different thing from a rewrite and must not be counted as one. That it strikes intermittently is the reason to flag it and not to wait: a duck that slips sometimes is harder to understand than one that always does.

music.label: YouTube
music.note: Writes back ITS OWN saved volume value after a duck, not the value that applied before it. Without this field the rewrite matches no known signature, reads as the user raising the volume, and the duck is released silently. The flag tells the tap to count every raise during a running duck as the player, whatever the value — the protection for the user then rests entirely on tempo, via RAPID_REASSERT_MS.

verified.note: The spread is the whole point. A time window was tried first and was not enough: set to 12000 ms the duck slipped anyway, because that time the rewrite came after 14161 ms. The delay appears to depend on where in a periodic reconciliation of ~15 s our change lands, not on a debounce — and a cycle time that has not been measured must not be guessed into a number in the registry. Hence a flag and no figure. The value written back was 0.32 in a live run where the duck went from 0.96; in an isolated measurement 0.95 was written after a change from 0.95, which at first made the two signatures look identical.
